content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.2) — model tends to lag or underreact to sentiment-driven rallies.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment or sentiment < 0.1) — model often fails to capture downward momentum or panic-driven drops.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model tends to overcorrect or overreact to recent highs, especially if sentiment is positive but volatile.
- Mean-reversion bias in medium-term forecasts — model frequently forecasts prices to revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too low in early stages of upward trends (especially if sentiment is rising) — model underestimates breakout potential.
- Lag in sentiment response: model often reacts to sentiment shifts 2–3 days after they occur — adjust forecasts to align with sentiment momentum rather than lagging indicators.
